extracted.intended_audience: readers of political theology and Christian subjects; students of early-modern political philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria from a political‑theological treatise about what is necessary for reception into the Kingdom of Heaven, the limits of pastoral (Papal) power, and how Christians ought to relate faith to obedience to civil sovereigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish commands of God from commands of men
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man receiveth two contrary Commands, and knows that one of them is Gods, he ought to obey that, and not the other, though it be the command even of his lawfull Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The difficulty lies in discerning whether a command given in God's name is truly from God or an abuse of God's name by false prophets/teachers. The rule: obey God's command if known to be from God; if not clearly God's, defer to lawful sovereign. Examples: false prophets in Jewish/Christian churches; warning that false teachers may use pretended revelation for private ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only two virtues are necessary to Salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is NECESSARY to Salvation, is contained in two Vertues, Faith in Christ, and Obedience to Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience here includes repentance (the will to obey) and Faith includes belief that Jesus is the Christ. Because of original and actual sin, remission of sins (reward of faith) is required as well. Nothing else is strictly necessary for salvation beyond these two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience required is the will/endeavour to obey
rubrics_metrics.description: The Obedience required at our hands by God, that accepteth in all our actions the Will for the Deed, is a serious Endeavour to Obey him; and is called also by names signifying that Endeavour (Charity, Love, Righteousnesse, Repentance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfeigned desire to fulfil God's commandments, sincere repentance, and love to God and neighbour count as the obedience necessary for reception into the Kingdom of God. God accepts the will for the deed in the faithful; perfect innocence is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: What laws are laws of God
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laws of God therefore are none but the Laws of Nature, whereof the principall is, that we should not violate our Faith, that is, a commandement to obey our Civill Soveraign, which wee constituted over us by mutuall pact one with another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ gave counsel, not new positive laws; the Sermon on the Mount expounds Mosaic law rather than creates a new civil code. The Bible is law only where the civil sovereign has made it so; in other places it is counsel. Thus obedience to civil law (properly constituted) is obedience to God's law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person to be believed — lawful pastors and supreme pastor
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary cause of beleeving that the Scriptures are the Word of God is the Hearing of those that are by the Law allowed and appointed to Teach us (Parents, Pastors); the Person which all they that have no speciall revelation are to beleeve, is (in every Common-wealth) the Supreme Pastor, that is to say, the Civill Soveraigne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith ordinarily comes 'by hearing' lawful teachers. Reputation of pastors and the authority of those who established Scripture undergird belief. Where revelation is absent, the lawful civil/supreme pastor is the final authoritative source for public doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith is ultimately a gift of God though mediated by teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith is the gift of God; he worketh it in each severall man, by such wayes, as it seemeth good unto himself. Nevertheless because he gives it ordinarily by the means of Teachers, the immediate cause of Faith is Hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should not conflate 'knowing' with 'believing'. Even when teaching produces belief, faith remains a divine gift; some taught profit, others do not. Claiming private inspiration makes one a prophet subject to examination by the church.

rubrics_metrics.name: The only strictly necessary article of Christian faith: 'Jesus is the Christ'
rubrics_metrics.description: Onely Article of Faith, which the Scripture maketh simply Necessary to Salvation, is this, that JESUS IS THE CHRIST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments provided: (a) scope of the evangelists centers on establishing Jesus as Christ; (b) Apostolic preaching proclaimed that 'there is another King, one Jesus'; (c) the easiness of the doctrine (e.g., the thief on the cross); (d) clear scriptural texts (John 20:31, 1 John 4:2) make this article sufficient for eternal life. Other doctrines are either implicit consequences or deductions from this foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easiness of required doctrine indicates limited necessary belief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thief upon the Crosse though repenting... could not have been saved for saying... only that Jesus Was The King. Therefore more than that is not Necessary; 'Christs yoke is Easy, and his burthen Light.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many complex/doctrinally disputed points were necessary, Christianity would be excessively difficult. Emphasizes that core belief required for salvation is accessible to simple believers and children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural texts showing sole necessity of belief in Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Places such as John 5:39, John 11:26, John 20:31, 1 John 4:2, Acts 8:36–37 show that believing Jesus is the Christ (or confessing him) is sufficient for eternal life and baptism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, uncontroversial scriptural passages rather than obscure texts when determining what faith requires. Where passages clearly equate belief in Christ with life, treat that as authoritative for necessary belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith plus repentance (obedience) is required for baptism and salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: Repentance, and Baptisme... ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. Thus Repentance, and Baptisme, that is, beleeving that Jesus Is The Christ, is all that is Necessary to Salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Acts 2 (Peter's preaching) and Luke 18 (commandments and reliance on Christ) indicate that both repentance (obedience/justice) and belief in Christ jointly suffice. 'Repent and Beleeve the Evangile' is the apostolic call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both Faith and Obedience contribute to justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith and Obedience are both Necessary to Salvation; when said that we are Justified by Works it means the will/endeavour (not perfect performance); when said justified by Faith it means faith makes our plea acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify terms: 'justified by works' refers to being denominated just because of the will to obey; 'justified by faith' refers to God accepting the plea through faith. Both senses reconcile apparent disputes about the basis of justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to civil sovereign compatible with obedience to God when sovereign is Christian
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Civill Soveraign bee a Christian, he alloweth the beleefe of this Article... and because he is a Soveraign, he requireth Obedience to all his owne, that is, to all the Civill Laws; in which also are contained all the Laws of Nature, that is, all the Laws of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus obeying a Christian sovereign does not hinder obedience to God. Even if a sovereign deduces false consequences, subjects and pastors who believe the foundation are still saved. Private judgment should not supersede the sovereign's authority in matters of obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to an infidel sovereign — internal faith permitted, rebellion sinful
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Civill Soveraign is an Infidel, every one of his own Subjects that resisteth him, sinneth against the Laws of God (for such as are the Laws of Nature), and rejecteth the counsell of the Apostles... And for their Faith, it is internall, and invisible; They have the licence that Naaman had, and need not put themselves into danger for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects should keep faith privately and not make war on an infidel sovereign; martyrdom for faith is allowed but not required. Resisting lawful sovereigns is normally sinful unless obedience would incur eternal damnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of pastoral (Papal) coercive power
rubrics_metrics.description: The last of these Powers [given to a Pastor] is no more than the Power, or rather Command to Teach... our Saviour refused to take upon him that Power in this world himself, but advised to let the Corn and Tares grow up together till the day of Judgment: much lesse did hee give it to St. Peter, or can S. Peter give it to the Popes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pastoral power consists chiefly in teaching. The Pope has no divinely granted coercive power to depose or coerce Christian kings; examples of priests or bishops exercising temporal power do not establish a right to such authority. Pastors may admonish but not exercise sovereign coercion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about precedent/examples as proof of right
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples prove nothing; Secondly, that the Examples he allegeth make not so much as a probability of Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances cited (Jehoiada killing Athaliah, Ambrose excommunicating Theodosius, actions by popes) are either exceptional, criminal, or void when done in their own cause. Therefore historical examples do not reliably establish juridical or divine right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret scripture by author's scope and main design
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the bare Words, but the Scope of the writer that giveth the true light, by which any writing is to bee interpreted; and they that insist upon single Texts, without considering the main Designe, can derive no thing from them cleerly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid atomizing scripture into isolated texts; interpret passages in the harmony of the whole Bible and according to the writer's main purpose. Anti-pattern: 'casting atomes of Scripture' to obscure truth or advance private advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret references to 'kingdom of darkness' allegorically
rubrics_metrics.description: Beelzebub is Prince of Phantasmes, Inhabitants of his Dominion of Air and Darknesse... the Children of Darknesse, and these Daemons, Phantasmes, or Spirits of Illusion, signifie allegorically the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to the 'kingdom of darkness' and princes of the air should be read allegorically as referring to phantasms, illusions, or spiritual rulers of error rather than physical polity. This affects how one understands moral/spiritual adversaries in theological-political discourse.
